tagline: Seven miles of shore road, seven centuries of royal Kona.
intro: Aliʻi Drive starts on the Kailua waterfront and runs about seven miles down the shore to Keauhou, two lanes all the way, roughly on the line of the ala loa, the old foot trail along the coast. Four of the seven ancient royal centers of Kona sit on it.

Kamehameha the Great lived out his last years at Kamakahonu, beside Kailua Pier, until his death in 1819. The first Christian missionaries came ashore at the same spot in 1820, and the church they founded, Mokuaikaua, was rebuilt in lava rock and crushed coral mortar between 1835 and 1837.

moments.title: Huliheʻe Palace
moments.text: Built of lava rock in 1838 for Governor Kuakini, the palace later belonged to Princess Ruth Keʻelikōlani, who preferred to sleep in a grass hut on the grounds.

moments.title: Holualoa Bay
moments.text: Oral tradition says Kamehameha I learned to excel at board and canoe surfing in these waters, beside a royal center that Aliʻi Drive split in two when it was first built.

moments.title: Kahaluʻu Bay
moments.text: An old breakwater called Pa o ka menehune, the wall of the ancients, may once have nearly closed the bay, and green turtles are still found in it.
